agent: ministers wave, reader D (the production script's provinces and buildings)
question: What each engine method the production minister's building code reaches answers - CBuildingDataBase.GetBuilding, CBuilding:GetIndex, CProvince GetBuilding/HasBuilding/GetCurrentConstructionLevel/IsFrontProvince/GetController/GetOwner/GetProvinceID, CProvinceBuilding:GetMax, CCountry GetTotalCoreBuildingLevels/GetRandomUnderGroundTarget - and what CConstructBuildingCommand's and CConstructConvoyCommand's Lua constructors take and IsValid tests.

addresses.name: CBuildingDataBase_GetBuilding
addresses.comment: **The Lua static `CBuildingDataBase.GetBuilding(name)`.** Copies the C string into a local std::string, makes g_CBuildingDataBase (0x1A870D4) if it does not exist yet, and answers StringHashFind_At1C(database, name) - the building whose key (CBuilding +0x1C) is exactly that string, **case and all**, or **null** where none is. luabind pushes a null pointer as nil, so `CBuildingDataBase.GetBuilding("infrastructure")` - which `ai_support_functions.lua`'s `Build_Infrastructure` asks for in Their Finest Hour, the base game and BlackICE alike, where every buildings.txt calls it `infra` - is **nil**. That path is dead in Their Finest Hour: no country file calls `Support.Build_Infrastructure` and `Utils.GetFunctionReference` never falls back to Support. Bare `ret`, one reference (the luabind registration at 0x906F78). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x8E9F80-0x8EA02E: strlen loop, std::string::assign (0x40A160) on [ebp-0x2c], the lazy `new 0x30` of [0x1A870D4], then `mov eax,[0x1a870d4]; push &string; call 0x4B8B60` (StringHashFind_At1C, recorded exact and case-sensitive, answers null on a miss), and `mov eax, esi` its answer returned through a bare `ret`. The four buildings.txt files (base, TFH, BlackICE) each have `infra = {` and no `infrastructure` key. Wrong if StringHashFind_At1C lowered the key, which its own record's byte compare rules out.

addresses.name: ReturnDword_0x54
addresses.comment: `mov eax,[ecx+0x54]; ret` - the whole body. Registered six times in luabind: as **CBuilding:GetIndex** (CBuilding +0x54, the building's index into a province's building array, which is the file's position + 1: air_base 1 .. infra 11 in Their Finest Hour) and as GetOwnerAI of all five AI ministers. A fold, so it is named for no class (trap 4); the field reading is the useful half. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x8E90A0: two instructions. luabind.json gives address 0x8E90A0 to CBuilding.GetIndex and to CAIPoliticsMinister/CAITechMinister/CAIEspionageMinister/CAIProductionMinister/CAIForeignMinister.GetOwnerAI; vtable.py --holding says no table holds it. The CBuilding +0x54 index is already recorded and is what CProvince::GetBuilding indexes with.

addresses.name: CProvinceBuilding::GetMax
addresses.comment: **Lua `CProvinceBuilding:GetMax()`: the level built, `level_max` (+0x20), in thousandths** - not the working level (+0x24, `level_current`, which bombing lowers and the day's repair fills). So a level just delivered, still at nought working, already counts, and a bombed level counts whole. `ret 4`, the hidden out pointer the one stack argument. One reference, its registration. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x417A70-0x417A7C: `mov ecx,[ecx+0x20]; mov eax,[ebp+8]; mov [eax],ecx; ret 4`. CProvinceBuilding +0x20 is recorded level_max and the Lua half names it Max (+0x24 Current). findRefs: one reference (0x8EC150, the registration), no vftable holds it.

addresses.name: CProvince::GetBuilding
addresses.comment: **Lua `CProvince:GetBuilding(building)`**: `this->+0x310[building->+0x54]` - the province's own CProvinceBuilding for that building, unchecked. Every province holds one for every building in the database (index 0 nobuilding), so a building the province has none of answers an object at level 0, never nil. **A nil building is not refused**: it is dereferenced at +0x54, an access violation and not a Lua error (luabind's pointer argument takes nil as null, inferred from the constructor invoker's identical test at 0x97F8F2). `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4A3B60-0x4A3B73: `mov eax,[ebp+8]; mov edx,[eax+0x54]; mov eax,[ecx+0x310]; mov eax,[eax+edx*4]; ret 4`, no test. That every element is a live object: CCountry::RebuildNeighbours walks each owned core province's whole +0x310..+0x314 array every day dereferencing each element's +0x18 definition with no null test (0x4E2B90-0x4E2BC1), as do HasBuilding and CHasBuildingTrigger. Wrong if some province's array were shorter than the database - nothing seen indexes it with a bound.

addresses.name: CProvince::HasBuilding
addresses.comment: **Lua `CProvince:HasBuilding(building)`: the level built above nought** - `buildings[building->+0x54]->level_max (+0x20) > g_FixedZero`, signed. So a level just delivered and not yet working counts, and so does a bombed one; a level only queued does not. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4A3900-0x4A391F: `mov eax,[ecx+0x310]; mov edx,[building+0x54]; mov eax,[eax+edx*4]; mov ecx,[eax+0x20]; cmp ecx,[0x1A870F4]; setg al; ret 4`. 0x1A870F4 is g_FixedZero (rva 0x16870F4), recorded as never written.

addresses.name: CProvince::GetCurrentConstructionLevel
addresses.comment: **Lua `CProvince:GetCurrentConstructionLevel(building)`: how many of that building are still to come on the first line queued for it in this province - in the province's OWNER's queue.** countries[this->owner id (+0x330)]->Constructions (+0xF40), head to tail: the first line whose slot 16 says it is a building line, whose location (+0x44) is this province and whose building (+0x58) is this one answers its `size` (+0x40, a whole count, not thousandths); none answers 0. Only the first match, where CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed sums every one. **The owner, not the controller and not the asker**: in a province the asking country controls but does not own its own lines are not seen - the owner's located lines there are cancelled the next day (CBuildingConstruction slot 12), so the answer is 0 whatever the asker has queued. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4A3930-0x4A399E: `mov eax,[ebx+0x330]` then `[0x1A855A4]+0x16C` (the country array) indexed by it, `mov edi,[eax+0xF40]`, the node walk `esi=[edi]; edi=[edi+8]`, `call [vft+0x40]` (slot 16), `cmp [esi+0x44],ebx` (ebx = this), `cmp [esi+0x58],building`, and `mov eax,[esi+0x40]` on the first hit; `xor eax,eax` at the end. Wrong if +0x330 were not the owner's id - it is the recorded owner tag's id half.

addresses.name: CProvince::IsFrontProvince
addresses.comment: **The game's own name, out of the Lua API (`CProvince:IsFrontProvince(bool)`)** - recorded until 2026-10-16 as CProvince::HasHostileLandNeighbour, which says the same thing. Body 0x4A56B0-0x4A57C9, `ret 4`. **False at once for a province nobody owns** (owner id +0x330 == 0) or with no edges. Then over the template's edges (+0x90/+0x94, 0x14 bytes each), in order, skipping: an edge of kind 3 (impassable) - **a kind-1 sea crossing counts**; a neighbour that is not land (template +0x22); a neighbour whose area (+0x2B4) answers slot 0 false, i.e. a CNullOwnerArea - land nobody owns; a neighbour with **this province's controller** (+0x338). The first neighbour left whose controller is an enemy of this province's controller answers true - CCountry::IsEnemy's province overload (0x42F210, the neighbour's controller in ESI, &this->controller in EDX, **this** province in EDI): the two at war (status +0x20), either of them REB, or an undeclared war between them (status +0x24) whose regions include **this** province. **With `requireLandUnits` set**, that neighbour must also hold at least one land unit (CountLandUnitsInList over its +0x2B8, every unit there whoever owns it, CUnit slot 15 IsLand); otherwise the walk goes on. The production script passes false: a front province is one touching enemy-held land by land or strait, garrisoned or not. 14 direct callers in C++ (the invasion planner, the theatre seats, UnitCanReachObjectiveOverland). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
addresses.revises: name CProvince::HasHostileLandNeighbour -> CProvince::IsFrontProvince (its luabind registration's name); confidence likely -> confirmed; the bool is named requireLandUnits (it counts every land unit in the neighbour, not a garrison of the enemy's); the comment adds the sea crossing counting, the undeclared war tested against this province, and the REB case
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4A56B0-0x4A57C9 read whole: `cmp [edi+0x330],0` -> false; edge count `(end-begin)/0x14`; `cmp [eax+edx],3; je skip`; neighbour `[[0x1A8557C]+0x2200][edge+4]`; `cmp byte [tmpl+0x22],0; je skip`; `mov ecx,[ebx+0x2B4]; call [[ecx]]` -> skip on false; `cmp [ebx+0x338],[edi+0x338]; je skip`; esi = countries[neighbour controller id], `lea edx,[edi+0x334]`, edi = this, `call 0x42F210`; `cmp byte [ebp+8],0; je true`; else `lea ecx,[ebx+0x2B8]; call 0x5D5C60; test eax,eax; jg true`. 0x42F210 listing 0x42F210-0x42F271: own id -> false, status[id]+0x20 -> true, either tag 'REB' -> true, then `test edi,edi`, status+0x24, `mov ecx,edi; call 0x4763A0` (UndeclaredWarCoversProvince). ProvinceEdge kind 1 is the recorded sea crossing. luabind.json registers 0x4A56B0 as CProvince.IsFrontProvince(CProvince const&, bool).

addresses.name: CCountry::GetTotalCoreBuildingLevels
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CCountry::GetTotalCoreBuildingLevels(CCountry* this, CFixedPoint* out, int buildingIndex)
addresses.comment: **Lua `CCountry:GetTotalCoreBuildingLevels(index)`**: element `index` of the vector at +0x1038/+0x103C, or 0 where `index` is not below its size (a negative index is not refused). It is a cache, filled only by CCountry::RebuildNeighbours (the daily rebuild and a change of hands): zeroed to one entry per building in the database, then **every owned province where the country holds a core** adds each building's `level_max` (built, not working), and then **every building line in the country's queue adds 1000 - one per line, whatever its size** - a line with no province always, a located line only where the country has a core in that province. So it answers built levels plus lines, as of the last rebuild; a line ordered since is not in it. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4E21A0-0x4E21D5: `(end-begin)>>2 > index` -> `[begin+index*4]`, else 0; `ret 8`. Its only writer is RebuildNeighbours by fieldchain --field 0x1038 (15 sites: the constructor 0x4C8A40, 0x4CA740 and RebuildNeighbours): the resize to `(db+0x10 - db+0xC)>>2` and zero at 0x4E252C-0x4E2674; the core walk 0x4E2A3B-0x4E2A5E (`[edi+0x344]` list, `cmp [node+4], country id`) into 0x4E2B86-0x4E2BC1 (`add [begin + def->+0x54 *4], [building+0x20]` for every element of +0x310..+0x314); the queue walk 0x4E2ED5-0x4E2F36 (slot 16, location null or a core node matching, `add [begin + building->+0x54 *4], 0x3E8`). Wrong if another writer existed outside the fieldchain hits; the positive control is that the same scan finds this reader at 0x4E21A9.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetRandomUnderGroundTarget
addresses.comment: **Lua `CCountry:GetRandomUnderGroundTarget()` - and it is not random.** Candidates, in order: if the country is a major (+0x15C) or MaxIC (+0x60C) is above 100, every province **owned** by each country of its Allies list (+0xF88, in list order, each ally's OwnedProvinces in list order); then its own OwnedProvinces (+0xCF0). A province qualifies where its underground (+0x30C) has `level_max` 0 (a line queued there does not stop it), its controller is not this country and is at war with it or either is REB, this country is a friend of its owner (CCountry::IsFriend with military access), and - for a minor - the owner is this country: Underground_CanPlaceIn's test, inlined. Each gets a weight `w = clamp(infra x (1000 + local_infra + global_infra) / 1000, 10, 1000) x 50 / 1000`, truncated - the province modifier's ids 12, 13, 14, the day's repair's roads figure; 0 to 50, five a level of infrastructure - **tripled for its own provinces**, an ally's taken once. Then **pick = 757147 mod (sum of weights)** - the immediate 0xB8D9B, no generator called - and the answer is the province id at that point of the cumulative weights. **0 where nothing qualifies or every weight is 0.** So for an unchanged map and infrastructure it answers the same province every time. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x509920-0x50A02D read whole (retsBefore gives its three exits, 0x509FE8, 0x50A00C, 0x50A02D, all of this body). Calls in the range: new, the game state's constructor, vector reserve/grow, IsFriend (0x4EF7C0) twice, floorf + _ftol2_sse (the static floor(10.5f) = 10 at 0x1BEA400), the 64-bit helpers, free - no RNG. The pick: 0x509F8F `mov eax,0xb8d9b; cdq; idiv ecx` with ecx the summed weights, then the walk 0x509FA6-0x509FC2 testing `c <= pick < c + byte[w]`. Own weight 3w at 0x509EE7-0x509EEB (`mov cl,al; add cl,cl; add al,cl`), ally weight w at 0x509C30. Wrong if 0xB8D9B were patched at load - it is an immediate in .text and the install's copy differs from the unpatched one only at the Patch_* sites (trap 19).

struct_fields.name: core_building_levels_begin
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a vector of one int per building in the database (indexed by CBuilding +0x54), thousandths: the summed built level (`level_max`) of each building over the provinces the country owns and holds a core in, plus 1000 for each building line in its queue that has no province or is in one of its core provinces - one per line, not per size. Rebuilt whole by CCountry::RebuildNeighbours (0x4E252C-0x4E2674 resize and zero, 0x4E2B86 the provinces, 0x4E2ED5 the lines); read by CCountry::GetTotalCoreBuildingLevels, the Lua API's. End at +0x103C, capacity at +0x1040. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section D.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldchain.py --field 0x1038: 15 sites - the constructor 0x4C8A40, 0x4CA740, RebuildNeighbours and GetTotalCoreBuildingLevels only. The listings at 0x4E2B86-0x4E2BC1 and 0x4E2ED5-0x4E2F36 add `[building+0x20]` and 0x3E8 at `begin + def->+0x54 * 4`; the decompile of RebuildNeighbours shows the same. Nothing is recorded between SpyingOnUs (+0x1028, a CCountryList) and num_of_ports (+0x105C).

struct_fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x1038 (core_building_levels_begin). GetTotalCoreBuildingLevels answers 0 for an index at or past it.
struct_fields.evidence: Listing 0x4E21A3-0x4E21B7: `(+0x103C - +0x1038) >> 2` compared with the index; RebuildNeighbours' resize at 0x4E2526-0x4E2654 pushes back to it with +0x1040 as the capacity.
